title_en: Elliott Appel: Caring for My Father Put My Life on Pause for 7 Years. Here’s What I Learne
title_zh: Elliott Appel：照顾父亲让我的人生按下七年暂停键——我学到的教训
subtitle_zh: 理财规划师 Elliott Appel 以照顾父亲的七年经历写书，分享 DPOA、财务防骗、照护机构选择与边界设定等实用指南。
summary_zh: 本期 The Long View 由 Christine Benz 与 Amy Arnott 对话理财规划师、Kindness Financial Planning 创始人兼作家 Elliott Appel，主题来自他照顾罹患四期肺癌父亲的七年经历与新书 How to Help Your Parents as They Age。Appel 的公司专注服务寡妇、照护者与经历重大健康事件的人群，他把电子表格式的税务、遗产规划与真实世界的情感权衡结合起来。节目给出大量即刻可用的实操建议：趁父母尚可自主决策时，逐家金融机构索取并使用它们各自格式的持久授权书（DPOA, durable power of attorney），以免日后审核推诿；把父母加进自己的手机套餐、准备一页纸的用药与住院清单；用老年照护顾问作为应对搬家等艰难对话的作弊码；重点防范掏空账户这类真正的大问题，而非纠结给伴侣的小额支出。Appel 反复强调照护者必须设定并动态调整自己的边界，并主张把遗产规划像体检一样强制化、纳入优雅老去的一部分。是一集兼具个人故事与养老财务防骗指南的深谈。

turns.en: Hi and welcome to the Long View. I'm Christine Benz, Director of Personal Finance and Retirement Planning for Morningstar. And I'm Amy Arnott, Portfolio Strategist for Morningstar.
turns.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听 The Long View。我是 Christine Benz，晨星（Morningstar）个人理财与退休规划总监。我是 Amy Arnott，晨星投资组合策略师。

turns.en: Our guest on the podcast today is Elliot Appel. He's a financial planner and the founder of Kindness Financial Planning. He's also an author.
turns.zh: 我们今天请到的嘉宾是 Elliott Appel。他是理财规划师，Kindness Financial Planning 的创始人，也是一位作家。

turns.en: His latest book is called How to Help Your Parents as They Age, a Financial Planner's Guide to Caregiving, which is a chronicle of his father's last years and the key lessons he learned along the way.
turns.zh: 他最新的一本书叫 How to Help Your Parents as They Age: A Financial Planner's Guide to Caregiving，记录了他父亲生命最后几年的经历，以及他一路学到的重要教训。

turns.en: He's also co-host of his own podcast called The Me and Money Podcast. I really love this conversation because Elliot provided so many tangible tips that people can use to help their parents.
turns.zh: 他还是自己播客 The Me and Money Podcast 的联合主持。我特别喜欢这期对话，因为 Elliott 给出了太多大家马上就能用在父母身上的实操建议。

turns.en: And his personal story really provides a lot of color. Yeah, so one of the concrete tips that I really liked was putting your parents on your own cell phone plan and why that can be really helpful if there's a lost phone or other issues that come up.
turns.zh: 他本人的故事也特别有色彩。对，我特别喜欢的一个具体建议，就是把父母加进你自己的手机套餐里——万一手机丢了或者出了别的问题，这一招非常管用。

turns.en: So, you know, my husband and I both have aging parents, so I've added that to my to-do list for the future. So let's get into the conversation.
turns.zh: 我和我先生家里都有上了年纪的父母，所以这条我已经列进我未来的待办清单了。那我们开始今天的对话吧。

turns.en: Elliot, welcome with a long view. Thanks, Christine. I appreciate you having me. Well, we're really glad to have you here and excited to talk about your book, which is wonderful.
turns.zh: Elliott，欢迎来到 The Long View。谢谢你，Christine，感谢邀请。我们很高兴你来，也很期待聊聊你的书，那是一本非常棒的书。

turns.en: We want to talk about the book and the backstory. But before that, can you talk about your work as a financial planner and what initially attracted you to that profession?
turns.zh: 我们想聊聊这本书和它背后的故事。不过在那之前，先谈谈你作为理财规划师的工作吧，最初是什么吸引你进入这个行业的？

turns.en: I loved financial planning because it married sort of the technical expertise of living in spreadsheets and planning and tax planning and estate planning with the real world and working with people.
turns.zh: 我热爱理财规划，因为它把技术层面的东西——整天泡在电子表格里做规划、税务规划、遗产规划——和真实世界、和与人打交道结合在了一起。

turns.en: And sometimes you would find the most common thing in a spreadsheet and maybe the most likely outcome isn't what someone wanted to do. And so I really loved when you got into it with people and you could sort of have the pros and cons of how is this actually going to work in the real world for people with emotions?
turns.zh: 有时候你会发现，电子表格里最常见的、最可能的结果，并不是那个人真正想做的事。所以我特别享受深入地和人们交流，一起权衡利弊：对一个有感情的人来说，这在现实世界里到底行不行得通？

turns.en: Your firm, which is called Kindness Financial Planning, focuses on widows, caregivers, and people affected by major health events. What made you want to home in on that as your specialty?
turns.zh: 你的公司叫 Kindness Financial Planning，专注于寡妇、照护者和受重大健康事件影响的人。是什么让你决定把这块作为你的专长？

turns.en: Yeah, so I worked for 10 years at a larger wealth management firm. And when I launched my own firm, I thought about the client conversations that I enjoyed the most.
turns.zh: 我在一家较大的财富管理公司工作了10年。当我创办自己的公司时，我回想了一下哪些客户对话是我最享受的。

turns.en: And there were many types of different folks I enjoyed working with. But in particular, widows or people going through major transitions, it just you could directly see the impact in real time of what sort of conversations and planning topics you were talking about and see sort of for the next generation too.
turns.zh: 我喜欢打交道的客户类型有很多，但尤其是寡妇或正在经历重大人生转变的人——你能实时、直接地看到那些对话和规划话题带来的影响，也能看到它对下一代的影响。

turns.en: I like working at the stage of life because you can start setting things up for that next generation and see the impact of that. And people are thinking about sort of what I would call maybe larger than life issues.
turns.zh: 我喜欢在人生的这个阶段工作，因为你可以开始为下一代做好安排，并亲眼看到这种影响。而且这个阶段的人们思考的，是我所说的比生命更宏大的议题。

turns.en: So legacy issues, like what do I want my impact to be in this world, those sorts of things? Exactly. How do I set my kids up? How do I make sure that they're well taken care of, but maybe not quote unquote spoiled and just make things easier for them too?
turns.zh: 比如传承问题：我想在这个世界上留下什么样的影响？就是这样。我怎么给孩子打好基础？我怎么确保他们被照顾得很好，但又不像所谓被宠坏，同时也让他们的生活更轻松？

turns.en: Maybe they had difficulties with their parents and settling their estates or not knowing what they wanted. And how do I make that easier for my heirs?
turns.zh: 也许他们自己在处理父母遗产、或不知道父母想要什么时遇到过困难，就会想：我怎么让继承人以后少走这种弯路？

turns.en: Okay. So we want to talk about the book, which really elegantly weaves your personal story with some really concrete advice about how people can help manage their parents' affairs.
turns.zh: 好，我们想聊聊这本书。它非常优雅地把你的个人故事和一些非常具体的建议编织在一起，教大家如何帮父母打理事务。

turns.en: So let's start with your personal story and maybe you can describe your relationship with your dad. It sounds like it was difficult in a lot of respects in contrast with your relationship with your mother, which was very good and loving.
turns.zh: 那就从你的个人故事开始吧，你能描述一下你和父亲的关系吗？听起来在很多方面都很艰难，和你与母亲那种非常好、充满爱的关系形成了鲜明对比。

turns.en: So maybe you can talk about your dad a little bit. Yeah. So I think difficult is a good word. Strained is one of the first words that came to mind with my dad.
turns.zh: 你能多讲讲你父亲吗？好，我觉得“艰难”这个词挺贴切。我想到父亲时，最先冒出来的词之一是“紧张”。

turns.en: And to give credit to my dad too, I mean, things did improve as I got older and we had a better relationship than I did when I was younger. But we tended to butt heads a lot.
turns.zh: 也得给我父亲说句公道话，随着我长大，情况确实好转了，我们的关系比年轻时更好。但我们还是经常起冲突。

turns.en: And as you look around as a kid, a teenager, a young adult, you sort of see other son, father relationships and you're like, that's just not the relationship I had with my dad.
turns.zh: 小时候、十几岁、成年早期，你环顾四周，看到别的父与子之间的关系，就会想：那根本不是我和我爸之间的关系。

turns.en: It just, he kind of showed up when it was convenient for him the most. And I think he struggled at times being a present dad. And so as he got sick, it was just an interesting thing to navigate with him.
turns.zh: 他总是在自己方便的时候才出现。我觉得他做不好一个在场尽责的父亲。所以他生病之后，和他怎么相处就成了一件非常复杂的事。

turns.en: And definitely of the generation of like, we're not talking about our feelings or not really doing anything along those lines. And so it made it hard when your dad's diagnosed with stage four lung cancer, where do you go from there?
turns.zh: 而且他肯定是那种“我们不谈感情”的一代人，完全不来那一套。所以当你的父亲被诊断出四期肺癌时，这让一切更难了——你该从何谈起？

turns.en: And that journey ended up being seven years and spanning cognitive impairment or broken hip and a lot of other things that I'm sure we'll talk about more.
turns.zh: 这段旅程最后长达七年，经历了认知障碍、髋骨骨折，还有很多别的事情，我确定我们后面会详细聊。

turns.en: Yeah. So without getting too much into the specifics of your dad's situation, can you kind of sum up what that period was like? And it sounds like your dad had an initial crisis and then a lot of other things.
turns.zh: 那我们不多说你父亲情况的具体细节，你能概括一下那段日子是什么样的吗？听起来你父亲先是经历了一次急性危机，然后又有别的事情

turns.en: Went wrong. Yeah. I think the best way to sum it up is just a roller coaster. I mean, a very acute cancer diagnosis. And then from there, he's essentially beat cancer.
turns.zh: 接连出错。是的，我觉得最好的概括就是过山车。先是极其凶险的癌症诊断，然后基本上他战胜了癌症。

turns.en: And then we went through cognitive impairment and some other situations. And I'll just, I'll keep it short there because I'm sure we'll talk about it more.
turns.zh: 接着我们又经历了认知障碍和一些别的情况。这些我先一带而过，我相信我们后面会展开聊。

turns.en: As I read through your dad's timeline from his diagnosis with lung cancer to his death, it occurred to me that he was mentally ill first and foremost.
turns.zh: 我沿着你父亲从确诊肺癌到去世的时间线读下来，意识到他首先是有精神疾病（mental illness）的。

turns.en: Did he ever receive an official diagnosis? He did not. And I actually messaged my mom as we were talking about the outline for that, just to double check to see if maybe there was something I missed.
turns.zh: 他得到过正式诊断吗？没有。我们讨论书的大纲时，我还专门问我妈妈确认了一下，看我是不是漏掉了什么。

turns.en: And she said that was an astute observation based on the book. You know, maybe, maybe he was narcissistic, anti-social, bipolar somewhere along those is maybe the, what we might suspect, but nothing official.
turns.zh: 她说这是个基于文本的敏锐观察。也许自恋型、反社会型、双相，大致在那些范围内，是我们可以猜测的，但从来没有正式诊断。

turns.en: And substance abuse was also in the mix. For sure. And my dad definitely struggled with substance use when I was a kid. But as far as I know, he, he was clean and did not touch anything for a long period of time.
turns.zh: 物质滥用也是一个因素。是的。我小时候，我父亲确实有过物质使用的问题。但据我所知，有很长一段时间他保持清醒，什么都没碰。

turns.en: And then sort of in the last few years of his life suffered a relapse. So as you mentioned, dementia was another big issue that your dad struggled with later in life.
turns.zh: 然后他在生命最后几年又复发了。所以正如你所说，痴呆（dementia）是你父亲晚年挣扎的另一个大问题。

turns.en: Do you think that his experiences and your experience in dealing with that situation are relevant to a lot of the adult children out there who are helping their parents through dementia or was his situation kind of unique and more complicated?
turns.zh: 你觉得你们应对他痴呆症的这段经历，对很多正陪伴父母走过痴呆的成年子女有参考价值吗？还是说他情况太特殊、太复杂了？

turns.en: I'm going to go with both as the answer there. It's definitely relevant, but his situation was also more complicated. It's one of those situations where he never had a formal dementia diagnosis, but definitely people will label it cognitive impairment.
turns.zh: 这个问题我想说两者都是。它绝对有参考价值，但他的情况确实更复杂。他从没拿到过正式的痴呆诊断，但大家肯定会说那是认知障碍。

turns.en: And interestingly, he did a mocha exam, which sort of measures cognitive impairment. And we saw that go down significantly one year, and then the next year it went up again.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，他做过 MoCA 认知障碍筛查。有一年分数明显下降，第二年又升回去了。

turns.en: And so that was very confusing for us. So a lot of what my dad went through, we kind of yo-yoed with health. But the same thing happens for people who are going through cognitive impairment or dementia.
turns.zh: 这让我们非常困惑。所以我父亲的健康状况是这样上上下下的，但正在经历认知障碍或痴呆的家庭，也会遇到同样的起起落落。

turns.en: They're going to face some sort of path forward of what do we do for our loved ones? You know, how do we get them into an appropriate living situation?
turns.zh: 他们总要面对一条怎么走下去的路：我们为亲人做些什么？怎么帮他们找到合适的居住环境？

turns.en: At what point do we make that change? How do we get buy-in from them? So a lot of the issues that we faced with my dad, everybody else is going to face that's on a similar path.
turns.zh: 什么时候该做出改变？怎么征得他们的同意？我们在父亲身上遇到的这些问题，走类似路线的其他人都会遇到。

turns.en: So in the book, you talk about how your mother and you were aiming to help your dad. Your parents were divorced, but your mom was still quite involved in his life.
turns.zh: 书中你写到，你和母亲一心一意想帮助你父亲。你父母虽然离婚了，但你母亲仍然很深入地参与他的生活。

turns.en: You were an only child for your parents. Can you talk about being an only? How helped hindered made it hard to help your dad? Yeah, I'm very thankful. I was an only child.
turns.zh: 你是父母的独生子女。能聊聊“独生”这个身份是帮了你还是让事情更难吗？我很庆幸我是独生子女。

turns.en: I've talked to families who are not only children who have to go through siblings. Even if all the siblings are on the same page, it's still slower and harder to go through the motions of all that because you want to get buy-in from your siblings.
turns.zh: 我跟不是独生子女的家庭聊过，他们得和兄弟姐妹一起处理。就算所有兄弟姐妹都意见一致，要走完这些流程也更慢、更难，因为你希望得到兄弟姐妹的认可。

turns.en: You want to figure out the next step, path forward. You know, with my mom, it was just, hey, we'd have a conversation. Generally, we'd agree and we'd move forward with a plan.
turns.zh: 你想一起确定下一步、往前走的路线。和我妈妈呢，就是坐下来谈一谈，一般我们能达成一致，然后按计划推进。

turns.en: So it just, it made decisions easier. Things went quicker. Emotionally, it took less time. And we all know as caregivers that time is in short supply when we're going through that.
turns.zh: 所以做决定更容易，事情推进更快，情绪消耗的时间也更少。我们做照护的人都知道，那段时间时间是多么不够用。

turns.en: So anything that can help alleviate that in my mind is a good thing. And I just know with siblings and having heard stories, almost nobody's ever completely satisfied with the process.
turns.zh: 任何能减轻这一点的事，在我看来都是好事。而我听了那么多有兄弟姐妹的故事之后，几乎没人对整个过程完全满意。

turns.en: Or as I can say, most things that my mom and I faced together, we were satisfied with what we did, even if the outcome wasn't necessarily what we always wanted.
turns.zh: 或者说，我和妈妈共同面对的大多数事情，即便结果不一定是我们想要的，我们对自己做了什么都是满意的。

turns.en: So one thing that really comes through loud and clear in the book is the value of an elder care consultant and how working with someone in that capacity really helped you personally.
turns.zh: 书中有一点让我印象特别深刻，就是老年照护顾问（elder care consultant）的价值——与这样的人合作真的帮到了你。

turns.en: What kinds of things did the elder care consultant that you hired help you with? And how can people find someone who is well-qualified and good to work with?
turns.zh: 你们请的那位老年照护顾问帮你们做了哪些事？人们怎么才能找到一位靠谱、好合作的人？

turns.en: Yeah, our elder care consultant was literally a lifesaver. She was amazing in every respect of it. And the way that you can find them, just to hit on that first, there is an organization called the Aging Life Care Association that has elder care consultants listed.
turns.zh: 我们的老年照护顾问真的是救命恩人，各方面都棒极了。先说怎么找：有一个叫 Aging Life Care Association 的组织，上面列有老年照护顾问。

turns.en: I would say don't limit your search to that. Our elder care consultant in particular, as an example, is not listed on that website. She came recommended from, I think, someone my mom used to work with who had hired her.
turns.zh: 但我想说别把搜索局限于此。就拿我们那位顾问来说，她都不在那个网站上。她是妈妈以前的同事推荐的，那位同事雇过她。

turns.en: So look in your local community, look for reviews, look for people out there. And maybe you have to work with someone virtually. But in terms of things that she did, I mean, I don't know where the scope is supposed to start and end for her, but it was literally everything from, hey, my dad lost his phone.
turns.zh: 所以看看你所在的社区，查查评价，找找周围的人。也许你得不限于远程合作。至于她做过的事，我不知道她的工作边界应该到哪，但真的是事无巨细，比如“我爸手机丢了”。

turns.en: She went and purchased a new phone for him that day. It could be strategizing around conversations. We introduced her to my dad as a quote unquote friend because we knew he wouldn't necessarily be happy with us hiring one.
turns.zh: 她当天就跑去给他买了一部新手机。她也帮我们为一些对话出谋划策。我们向爸爸介绍她时，说的是“朋友”——因为我们知道，他要是知道我们雇了个人，肯定不高兴。

turns.en: And that suggestion of mentioning her as our friend came from that. Came from them. They made that suggestion. They also helped us tackle difficult conversations like when should my dad move?
turns.zh: 把她介绍成朋友这个主意，就是他们出的。他们还帮我们应对艰难对话，比如我爸什么时候该搬家？

turns.en: And what does that look like? How do you bring that up with him? So it was really whenever we were our backs against the wall and we had no idea what to do, we went to them.
turns.zh: 搬家会是什么样子？该怎么跟他开口？所以每当我们走投无路、完全不知道怎么办的时候，我们就去找他们。

turns.en: And that was really effective and helpful because they do this every day. This was our first time helping someone. So it's like, why not put in the cheat code of having the person who knows how to do this help you with it?
turns.zh: 这真的非常有效、非常有用，因为他们天天干这个，而我们第一次帮人走这条路。既然有懂行的人愿意教你，干嘛不用这个“作弊码”呢？

turns.en: Right. It sounds like getting buy-in from the person you're trying to help is important. I mentioned to Amy that a friend of mine had hired an elder care consultant to help her dad.
turns.zh: 对，听起来，从你想帮助的人那里获得认同很关键。我刚还跟 Amy 说起，我朋友雇了个老年照护顾问帮她爸爸。

turns.en: And the dad really pushed back. He felt like it was maybe an excess layer or a waste of money. If someone's in that situation, apart from maybe or in addition to using that trick of saying this is a friend, are there any other steps that one might take to get that buy-in from a parent?
turns.zh: 她爸爸非常抗拒，觉得这是多余的一层，或者浪费钱。如果有人遇到这种情况，除了——或者除了说“这是朋友”这个技巧之外——还有哪些办法能让父母点头？

turns.en: I'm not sure about the buy-in piece, but I would say that there's a lot that they can do behind the scenes also for you without necessarily providing direct care or being in communication with your loved one or parent.
turns.zh: “争取认同”这块我不太有把握，但我想说，就算不直接提供照护、不直接和你的亲人或父母沟通，他们在幕后也能为你们做很多事。

turns.en: So we actually hired our elder care consultant years before we ever introduced her to my dad and personally paid for her to help strategize around some of these things behind the scenes.
turns.zh: 实际上，我们在把这位顾问介绍给我爸爸之前好几年就雇了她，是我们自费请她在幕后帮我们就各种事情出谋划策。

turns.en: So I just want to provide that as another avenue that if your loved one is not willing to accept it, that's another avenue. But the other way to approach this too is to try to set boundaries of, Hannah, I want to do X, Y, Z thing.
turns.zh: 我想把这作为另一条路径提供给你：如果你的亲人不愿意接受，这也是一条路。另一个办法是试着划清边界：我想做某件事，

turns.en: I need some help personally. Can I hire them to do this thing for us? We also wanted to spend a bit of time talking about estate planning and financial matters.
turns.zh: 我个人需要一些帮助，我们能不能雇他们来做这件事？我们也想花点时间聊聊遗产规划和财务上的事。

turns.en: And you noted that your father did have some time following his cancer diagnosis to put an estate plan in place. What went right with that plan and what do you wish he had done differently?
turns.zh: 你提到你父亲确诊癌症后确实有过一段时间来落实遗产规划。那个规划里什么做对了？你希望他当时有什么不同的做法？

turns.en: Almost everything went right in the end, which I was very happy about. But I also will caution people who are listening to this is my dad had a really simple financial situation, so it was much easier for it to go simply.
turns.zh: 结果几乎一切都顺利，这让我非常欣慰。但我也要提醒听众：我父亲的财务状况非常简单，所以事情才能简单。

turns.en: The one thing I wish we had known about, and this is actually kind of funny, is two months ago, give or take, I got a letter from the state of Washington that my dad had a retirement account with them and my dad's been dead three years now.
turns.zh: 唯有一件我希望我们早点知道的事——说起来还有点好笑——大概两个月前，我收到华盛顿州的一封信，说我父亲在他们那儿有一个退休账户。而我父亲已经去世三年了。

turns.en: And it was just one of those annoying things that popped up of like, here's a couple hundred bucks that I now have to get notarized, signed forms, processed this.
turns.zh: 就是这种烦人的小事突然冒出来：这儿有几百美元，现在我还得去公证、签字、走流程。

turns.en: So it took a lot of extra time. I wish we had caught that account previously. I don't think he even knew about it at the time. So that'd be the only thing that I'd redo differently.
turns.zh: 那花了额外的很多时间。我真希望我们之前就把那个账户找出来。我觉得连他自己当时都不知道。所以那是唯一一件我想重做的事。

turns.en: And I wish my dad had started an estate plan prior to him becoming sick. So it was one last thing he had to do among the chaos of getting stage four lung cancer and going through the motions with that.
turns.zh: 我还希望我父亲在生病之前就开始做遗产规划。于是它就成了确诊四期肺癌、兵荒马乱那一堆事里最后一件他不得不办的事。

turns.en: So in the book, you have lots of valuable guidance about the estate planning documents that we all should have. And one of them is durable power of attorney, which exercises control over financial matters.
turns.zh: 书中你讲了很多我们每个人都该具备的遗产规划文件，其中一个就是持久授权书（durable power of attorney，DPOA），掌管财务事项。

turns.en: You talk about how that worked really well for you in terms of managing your dad's financial affairs. I was interested because in Beth Pinsker's really good book kind of along the same lines, she talks about how this was just a huge pain point for her.
turns.zh: 你说这份文件在你处理父亲财务时非常管用。我对此很感兴趣，因为 Beth Pinsker 那本同题材的好书写到，这件事对她来说曾是一场巨大的噩梦。

turns.en: So maybe you can talk about the different types of durable power of attorney and what people should be thinking about when they draft those documents.
turns.zh: 那你能讲讲持久授权书的不同类型，以及大家在起草这些文件时应该考虑什么吗？

turns.en: Yeah. And this can be a major pain point for a lot of people. Beth's experience is sort of the more common one. I will say that we had a durable DPA for my dad, which meant that it was effective immediately as opposed to a springing durable power of attorney, which usually there's certain actions that need to happen.
turns.zh: 这确实可能是很多人的大痛点，Beth 的经历其实是更常见的那种。我们给我爸用的是即行生效的持久授权书，而不是触发式（springing）DPOA——后者通常要先满足某些条件才生效。

turns.en: Usually one to two physicians certify that you're incapacitated and no longer have the judgment to make decisions for yourself. And I am not attorney, but I will say I don't love the springing durable power of attorneys out there because it's just one more burden to put on someone during an already hard time.
turns.zh: 通常要一到两名医生证明当事人已无行为能力、无法再做决定。我不是律师，但我会说我不太喜欢市面那些触发式 DPOA，因为在已经够艰难的时刻，它只会再压上一份担子。

turns.en: And in my experience, a lot of physicians don't necessarily want to declare someone incapacitated because it's taking away their rights. And there's often not a clear cut line of when someone is incapacitated, unless you're literally in the hospital and you can't talk.
turns.zh: 以我的经验，很多医生并不愿意宣判某人无行为能力，因为这等于剥夺他的权利。而且什么时候算无行为能力，往往没有清晰界线——除非人真的躺在医院里说不出话。

turns.en: When we're talking about cognitive impairment, typically there's a gray zone. It's not black or white in that situation. It depends on how your person is doing that day.
turns.zh: 说到认知障碍，通常存在一个灰色地带，不是非黑即白。这取决于你的亲人那一天状态如何。

turns.en: The one thing that we did too is we used the own financial institution's DPA forms as opposed to my dad's forms. And this meant that we knew it would get accepted.
turns.zh: 我们还做了一件事：用的是我们自己的金融机构的 DPOA 格式文本，而不是我父亲原来那份。这就意味着我们知道它一定会被受理。

turns.en: One of the main issues that people go through a lot of times is they'll submit the DPA for finances that their attorney prepared to the financial institution.
turns.zh: 人们经常碰到的一个大问题是：把律师起草的财务 DPOA 提交给金融机构，

turns.en: And it often goes through a lengthy review process. Sometimes there's pushback from the financial institution that they don't want to do it, or they want to see certain language.
turns.zh: 往往会经历漫长的审核，有时机构还会推诿不想认，或者要求看到某些措辞。

turns.en: And so we proactively throughout this process made sure that we used the specific financial institution's forms prior to my dad sort of having the cognitive impairment and everything else that happened.
turns.zh: 所以我们从一开始就主动确保，在我父亲出现认知障碍和其他状况之前，就用上了各家金融机构自己的格式文本。

turns.en: So if you're kind of planning ahead and you're trying to get the specific POA form from each financial institution, that might be kind of time consuming and tedious to go through.
turns.zh: 所以如果你提前规划，逐家金融机构去要它们自己的 POA 表格，那可能挺费时间、挺繁琐的。

turns.en: But it sounds like it would probably make things easier down the road. I strongly believe so. And I think it's one of those things that as you age, you don't necessarily have to be going through a crisis to add this.
turns.zh: 但听起来日后会省不少事。我完全同意。而且我觉得这是那种你年纪渐长时不必等到危机来了才补的事情。

turns.en: One of the conversations I have with clients of fair amount is as you get older, maybe let's just proactively add someone that you trust to this, or maybe your actual DPA and your legal documents.
turns.zh: 我和客户常聊的一个话题就是：随着你变老，不如主动把你信任的人加进去——加到你的 DPOA 和法律文件里。

turns.en: So it's set up to help when you need it as opposed to one more thing that we have to add later during a crisis. So if you already have a durable power of attorney set up and then you contact the financial institution to get their specific forms, how do those two things work together?
turns.zh: 这样它在你需要的时候就已经就位，而不是危机之中又要临时添加的一件事。那如果你已经设好了持久授权书，然后再联系金融机构拿他们自己的表格，这两者怎么配合？

turns.en: Yeah. So I'm sure an attorney might have different opinions on this. And I'd always say go back and consult your own specific attorney. I think the greatest fear maybe is you do all that careful planning with an attorney and you grant your agent specific powers within that DPA.
turns.zh: 律师们可能有不同意见，我总是说回去咨询你自己的律师。我觉得大家最大的顾虑是：你和律师仔细规划完，在 DPOA 里给了代理人某些特定权限。

turns.en: And then maybe you sign a financial institution specific DPA that maybe gives them more powers than you anticipated. The one that often comes up that people are afraid of is changing beneficiaries, for example.
turns.zh: 结果你在金融机构自己的 DPOA 上签了字，可能赋予了他超出你预期的权力。人们常担心、也最常碰到的一个例子，是变更受益人。

turns.en: Maybe you don't give that in your actual DPA document that you prepared with an attorney, but maybe you initial the financial institution that allows that.
turns.zh: 也许你和律师起草的那份 DPOA 里根本没给这个权限，但你在金融机构的表格上签了允许。

turns.en: So I think it's just being mindful of which powers you're granting and do they match. And I'm sure an attorney would have more things to say about this.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得关键就是留心你在授予哪些权力、两边是否一致。律师肯定有更多话要说。

turns.en: I just know from a financial planning perspective, it's worked really well when we use the specific form in advance. Your dad was often making riskier subpar choices, bad choices, and that extended to his financial accounts too.
turns.zh: 我只知道从理财规划的角度，提前用机构自己的表格，效果非常好。你父亲经常做出风险更高、更差的选择，在财务账户上也不例外。

turns.en: What advice do you have for adult children who want to try to protect their parents from making poor financial decisions or being scammed, especially if the parents are experiencing cognitive decline?
turns.zh: 对于那些想保护父母不乱做财务决定、不被骗的成年子女——尤其是父母已经开始认知衰退——你有什么建议？

turns.en: I think the best way to think about this is when you go rent a car, for example, at an airport and then I'll back up, we want to put up as many roadblocks as possible.
turns.zh: 我觉得最好的思路是：就像你在机场租车——我先说回来——我们要尽可能多地设置障碍。

turns.en: So when you rent a car and you have to exit the facility, there might be a gate, there might be spike strips, there might be roadblocks, you might have to go through some corners.
turns.zh: 你租车完要开出车场时，会有闸门、有阻车钉、有路障，还得绕过几个弯。

turns.en: We're basically just trying to put as many safeguards in place as possible. You're not going to fully be able to do everything to prevent that.
turns.zh: 我们 basically 就是在尽可能多地设置防护措施。你不可能做到万无一失。

turns.en: And I just want to get that out there at the start because I think all of us that are well-intentioned want to make sure they never fall victim to anything.
turns.zh: 我想一开始就把这句话说清楚，因为我们所有出于好意的人，都想确保他们永远不上当。

turns.en: We want to prevent the big things. So first thing that I would start is start having these money conversations and aging conversations early.
turns.zh: 我们要防的是大事。第一件事，就是尽早开始谈钱、开始谈衰老的对话。

turns.en: The more you can become a trusted partner in it, the more likely they are to turn to you for help. And this was very different between my mom and my dad.
turns.zh: 你越能成为他们信赖的伙伴，他们遇到事就越可能来找你。这一点在我爸妈身上非常不同。

turns.en: My dad didn't really turn to me for help for many things, whereas I have the relationship with my mom that if something is odd or off, she gives me a call to double check.
turns.zh: 我爸很多事从来不找我帮忙，而我和妈妈之间，如果有什么不对劲，她会打电话来跟我核实。

turns.en: Hey, what should we do as opposed to just doing it? Like sending money, for example, or a weird link in an email. So I think that's one. And then the other thing is to get set up on any accounts, whether that's a DPUA or if your parents aren't willing to do that at this point.
turns.zh: 她会问“我们该怎么办”，而不是先斩后奏——比如汇款，或者点来路不明的邮件链接。这是第一点。第二点是想办法拿到各账户的权限，不管是 DPOA，还是父母暂时不愿意的话，

turns.en: Maybe it's a view-only authorization form with a financial institution. Maybe it's setting up a budgeting software or something where you can see financial transactions.
turns.zh: 也许可以在金融机构签一个只读授权书，或者设一个你能看到交易流水的记账软件之类。

turns.en: It's not necessarily going to prevent it, but it will at least give you insight into what's happening in their financial institution. And that way, if something does go wrong, it's easier to step in to help.
turns.zh: 这未必能阻止事情发生，但至少让你了解他们在金融机构里的动态。这样万一出了问题，你更容易及时介入帮忙。

turns.en: Other low-hanging fruit here is to freeze their credit. I'm operating off the assumption that all of our personal information is out there. It's just a matter of time till someone gets it and uses it.
turns.zh: 还有一个唾手可行的事：冻结信用。我的预设是，我们所有人的个人信息都已泄露，只是时间问题会被谁拿去用。

turns.en: So let's stop any sort of new loan applications. And then stopping solicitations like the credit card offers or charity reminders in the mail.
turns.zh: 那就阻止一切新的贷款申请。再就是停掉各种推销，比如信用卡邀约、邮寄的慈善催捐信。

turns.en: Let's just put as many roadblocks in there as possible. So they're not tempted by those things, whether that's giving money away or signing up for something that they don't necessarily need.
turns.zh: 尽可能多设路障，让他们不抵挡不住诱惑——不管是送钱出去，还是签些根本不需要东西。

turns.en: So if you're an adult child with an aging parent, how do you balance setting up some financial guardrails and safeguards? For example, an aging parent might be making spending decisions that you don't agree with, like maybe they have a new boyfriend or girlfriend and they're giving that person money or they're spending a lot of money on a hobby or a new car or new boat.
turns.zh: 那身为有年迈父母的成年子女，你怎么在设置财务护栏和另一方面之间取得平衡？比如年迈的父母可能做出你不认同的消费决定——给新交的男朋友或女朋友钱，或者在某个爱好、新车、新游艇上一掷千金。

turns.en: So how do you kind of balance that with putting some safeguards in place but also realizing that the parent can still make their own decisions if you don't always agree with them?
turns.zh: 你怎么既设置防护措施，又接受父母仍然有权自己做决定——即便你并不总是认同？

turns.en: Yeah, that's a really, really hard one to do because as long as they have capacity, they can spend any which way they want. So I think it's a lot of internal soul searching for adult children to say, okay, my parents are going to do this.
turns.zh: 这真的非常难，因为只要他们还有行为能力，他们想怎么花就怎么花。所以成年子女要做很多内在的自我梳理：好，父母就是要这么做。

turns.en: I don't necessarily have any influence over that decision but maybe I can have conversations with them to better understand it. So if it does cross a line, I can figure out, does that fit with the philosophy or how they're thinking about it?
turns.zh: 我对这个决定可能没有影响力，但也许我可以和他们聊聊，更好地理解它。如果真越过了某条线，我才能判断：这符合他们的理念、他们一直以来的想法吗？

turns.en: And just trying to prevent those really big things because there's a big difference between maybe providing regular money to a boyfriend or a partner and completely draining an account to give it to someone else, right?
turns.zh: 尽量防住真正的大问题，因为定期给男朋友或伴侣一些钱，和把账户掏空全给别人，差别非常大。

turns.en: I think it's how do we prevent those really big things from happening and just make sure that they're aware what's the impact of the smaller decisions.
turns.zh: 我觉得重点是防止那些真正的大事发生，同时让他们意识到小决定的影响。

turns.en: So if you give your boyfriend, I don't know, $500 a month, is that really going to wreck their financial picture or is that an okay thing that they want to do?
turns.zh: 比如每月给男朋友 500 美元，这真的会毁掉你的财务吗？还是说这是你愿意做的、没问题的？

turns.en: You also make the point that a lot of the features that people can use to protect their kids' cell phones and online activities can also be helpful for a parent who has cognitive impairment.
turns.zh: 你还提到，人们用来保护孩子手机和上网行为的很多功能，对有认知障碍的父母同样好用。

turns.en: Can you talk a bit more about that? Yeah, this was a hard one maybe morally and ethically for me when we were doing it. It felt very uncomfortable at the time but as my dad was making really poor decisions and he lost his phone and we couldn't find it because he didn't have the find my phone feature activated, we decided to install some child protection software on it and this was a way to both find the phone in the future
turns.zh: 能多讲讲吗？这在我当时是个道德和伦理上挺难的抉择，做起来很不舒服。但我父亲一直在做很糟糕的决定，他又丢了手机，而我们找不到——因为他没开查找手机功能。于是我们决定在他手机上装了儿童保护软件。这样以后既能找到手机——

turns.en: which it actually did end up coming in handy later when he lost it again but also to be able to block communication. So there were certain people that we didn't necessarily want my dad communicating with because they were providing cocaine to him and so it was how do we block those communications and it just happens to be that the protection that you put on maybe a kid's cell phone is the same stuff that works really really well for adult parents.
turns.zh: 后来他真的又丢手机时，这招确实用上了——还能屏蔽通讯。有些人我们不想让他们再和我爸联系，因为在给他提供可卡因。所以怎么屏蔽这些通讯？碰巧，你给孩子手机上的保护设置，对年迈的父母同样非常好用。

turns.en: I wanted to go back to financial accounts and as an adult child, maybe a trusted adult child, what's the best way to provide oversight of what's going on with those accounts?
turns.zh: 我想回到财务账户的话题。作为值得托付的成年子女，监督这些账户动静的最好方式是什么？

turns.en: You caution against being listed as a co-owner on accounts. Maybe you can talk about why you don't think that's an optimal choice but what's a better way if someone wants to keep track of what's going on with the comings and goings in the checking account as well as in the investment accounts?
turns.zh: 你不建议被列为账户的共同持有人。能说说为什么那不是最优选择吗？如果想盯着支票账户和投资账户的进出，更好的做法是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, the ideal way for me is to add it as that agent for the durable power of attorney for finances because it's going to give the ability to move money and help with the account.
turns.zh: 我认为最理想的方式是以财务持久授权书代理人的身份加入，因为它能让你有权调动资金、打理账户。

turns.en: So let's say your parent is hospitalized and you need to pay a bill on their behalf and you want to pay it out of the account, you'll actually be able to do that.
turns.zh: 比方说你父母住院了，你需要替他从账户里付一笔账单，你真的可以做到。

turns.en: The next step down, a lot of financial institutions have a view-only authorization where you can view what's going on but it's not actually going to give you the ability to do anything in the account.
turns.zh: 次一级的方式是很多金融机构提供只读授权：你能看到账户动态，但不能实际操作账户。

turns.en: So that would be, hey, my parents aren't necessarily comfortable adding me but I want to see what's going on and help monitoring it in your scenario.
turns.zh: 那种情形就是：父母还不太愿意加我，但我想看看发生了什么、帮忙盯着。

turns.en: And then sort of the last thing would be a trusted contact on an account which isn't going to give you any visibility into something that happens but if the financial institution suspects there's an issue or there's fraud or something else going on, it gives them the ability to call you.
turns.zh: 最后一种方式是在账户上设一个信任联系人（trusted contact）。它不给你任何账户可见性，但如果金融机构怀疑出了问题或有欺诈，他们可以打给你。

turns.en: It's not my favorite but it is a good sort of last line of defense and then your question about why would I not put my child or my parent on the same account as a joint account holder.
turns.zh: 这不是我的首选，但确实是最后一道防线。然后是你刚才问的：为什么我不把孩子或父母加为账户共同持有人。

turns.en: I would not do that because you're introducing new risk for your parent. So if you add your adult child as an additional account holder, if they get divorced, if they get brought into a lawsuit, if they have creditors they can't pay, that money can be brought in.
turns.zh: 我不会这么做，因为这给父母引入了新的风险。加上成年子女做共同持有人后，如果他们离婚、吃官司、有还不清的债务，这笔钱可能被牵连进去。

turns.en: And I think a lot of people have good intentions with this. They say, okay, it's a small checking account. I'm going to add them just to help pay bills.
turns.zh: 很多人初衷是好的：就是个小额支票账户，我加他进来只是为了帮忙付账单。

turns.en: There's only ever a small amount in there but I remember really vividly talking to an attorney once about this and they told me a story about how that same exact scenario, it was supposed to be a small account but unfortunately some home proceeds got deposited into the supposedly small account and never got moved to an investment account as they anticipated.
turns.zh: 里面永远只有很少的钱。但我清楚记得有次和一位律师聊到这个，他讲了个一模一样的故事：本来也是小账户，结果一笔卖房款阴差阳错打进了那个“小”账户，再也没按计划转到投资账户。

turns.en: The person ended up dying and then all of the home proceeds and we're talking north of $500,000 went to that sibling and that never got shared among the siblings.
turns.zh: 后来当事人去世，那笔卖房款——超过 50 万美元——全归了那一个子女，从来没在兄弟姐妹间分配。

turns.en: It just went to that person in particular. So I think a lot of people operate off the assumption that what's happening today is what will happen in the future but that doesn't always happen.
turns.zh: 就那样全给了那个人。所以很多人默认今天什么样、将来就什么样，但事情不一定如此。

turns.en: So we want to put processes and systems in place so if the out of the ordinary happens, we're not subjecting ourselves to strange family dynamics or money going to places we don't want them.
turns.zh: 我们要建立流程和机制，这样意外发生时，我们才不会受制于奇怪的家庭纠葛，钱也不会流向我们不想它去的地方。

turns.en: As a financial advisor, you've got your clients back and we've got yours. With Vanguard's actively managed bond funds, you're backed by consistent performance with a low cost edge for an advantage that keeps compounding and compounding and compounding and- Sorry, quick break for legal.
turns.zh: 作为理财顾问，你有客户的托付，我们也有你的托付。先锋集团的主动管理债券基金，以一贯稳健的业绩和低费率优势为你护航，让优势不断复利、复利、复利……抱歉，暂停一下做个法律声明。

turns.en: To learn more, visit vanguard.com slash audio. All investing is subject to risk. Investments and bonds are subject to interest rate, credit and inflation risk Vanguard Marketing Corporation distributor.
turns.zh: 了解详情请访问 vanguard.com/audio。所有投资都有风险。债券投资面临利率风险、信用风险和通胀风险。承销商：Vanguard Marketing Corporation。

turns.en: And compounding and compounding and compounding. Are you backed by institutional quality bond funds? Vanguard. You also mentioned the idea of the adult child putting the parents on the adult child's cell phone plan.
turns.zh: 复利、复利、再复利。机构级品质的债券基金为你护航。先锋。你还提到过成年子女把父母加进自己手机套餐的这个主意。

turns.en: What pain points does that help circumvent? Yeah, so all my stories come from a personal pain point that I experienced in this one. In particular, I remember my dad lost his phone.
turns.zh: 它能绕开哪些痛点？我的每个故事都来自一个我亲身经历过的痛点。这个我印象特别深：我爸把手机弄丢了。

turns.en: He was hospitalized and I spent a good portion, at least half a day, running around to get my dad a new phone. I was not on his plan. He's in the hospital.
turns.zh: 他当时住院，我花了至少半天时间到处跑给他配新手机。我不在他的套餐账户上。他在医院。

turns.en: We had to get the elder care consultant involved. We had to get a sign note by my dad, a driver's license or an ID copy. I had to bring that to the store, which of course was across town.
turns.zh: 我们只好把老年照护顾问拉进来，要我爸写一张签字便条，附上驾照或身份证复印件。我得把材料送到店里——当然还在城的另一头。

turns.en: Bring that in, get added to the account, and then have the elder care consultant go purchase the phone. Whereas if we were just on the same cell phone plan, or I was an authorized representative on his, it would have been a really simple phone call to get this all resolved and accessed to his account.
turns.zh: 交材料、被加进账户，然后让照护顾问去买手机。而如果我们在同一个手机套餐上，或者我是他账户的授权办理人，一个电话就能搞定，还能直接进他的账户。

turns.en: But he didn't know the pin because he forgot it. He didn't have his phone. It was like the storm that was perfect. And it was all for a new cell phone.
turns.zh: 但他不知道 PIN 码，密码也忘了，手机又不在身边，简直是一场完美风暴。而这一切只是为了买一部新手机。

turns.en: And that took up half a day. And so I think it's whether it's a utility bill, a cell phone plan, something like that. All these people who are hard to talk to unless you're on the account, I'd recommend getting at it in some capacity.
turns.zh: 那占了半天时间。所以不管是水电账单、手机套餐还是类似的：所有这些不挂在账户上就很难对接的人和机构，我建议你想办法以某种方式挂进去。

turns.en: In the book, you discuss a lot of professionals that one might hire to help with various aspects of this. One was a daily money manager. Can you talk about what that is and in what situations hiring one might be the right call?
turns.zh: 书中你写到很多可能请来的专业人士。其中一个是日常账务管理员（daily money manager）。能讲讲这是什么、什么情况下请一位合适吗？

turns.en: Yeah. Think about this person as the person that can, one, primarily help pay bills. Now, I hope most people have as many things on auto pay as possible.
turns.zh: 你可以把这个人想象成：首先，主要帮忙付账单。我希望大多数人已经把能自动扣款的都自动了。

turns.en: And that's a big thing that when I talk to older folks, some are resistant to that. But I think we can make some progress there. But then make sure things like medical claims were processed correctly.
turns.zh: 我和老年人聊的时候，有些对自动扣款很抵触，但我想这可以慢慢推动。另外还要确保医疗理赔等处理得正确。

turns.en: They can help sort mail with your loved one. They can sit down and help them pay those bills together if they don't want to put it on auto pay.
turns.zh: 他们可以陪着你的亲人整理邮件；如果不想自动扣款，他们可以坐下来陪着一起账单付款。

turns.en: They can reconcile accounts, organize tax documents. Think about this as sort of the administrative person that is helping your loved one. And they have some credentials and some safeguards behind that in helping them.
turns.zh: 他们能帮对账、整理税务文件。就把它想成给亲人做“行政助理”的人，背后有相应资质和保障措施。

turns.en: I think it's really helpful to hire them when it's clear that your loved one can't handle it or starts to become an issue and you don't necessarily want to step in and or your loved one doesn't necessarily want you involved in their finances at that point.
turns.zh: 当很明显你的亲人已经应付不了、或者账单开始出问题时——而你不方便亲自出面，或者亲人那阶段不想让你掺和财务——请这个人就非常有用。

turns.en: It's one of those things where if you have the ability to do it, your parent trusts you, I'd say hop in and do that. But our time is stretched thin.
turns.zh: 如果你自己能做、父母也信任你，我会说你干脆上手做。但我们的时间精力都被拉得很紧。

turns.en: So as much as you can outsource certain things so you can focus on maybe more important things, then you have to weigh sort of when that makes sense.
turns.zh: 所以能外包就外包，把精力留给更重要的事，什么时候划算要自己权衡。

turns.en: The book also includes a lot of detail about managing health care for a parent. And one thing you discuss is helping with decisions about when and where a parent should be discharged after a hospital stay.
turns.zh: 书里还有很多篇幅讲父母的医疗管理，其中一个话题是帮助决定住院后何时、转去哪里出院。

turns.en: What should people know about managing those transitions? Yeah, for us, this was kind of a wild, wild West and always a wild card scenario because at the end of the day, a social worker would ask us, you know, what is the proper place for my dad or what does that look like?
turns.zh: 对这些转介，大家该知道些什么？对我们来说，这基本是蛮荒西部，永远充满意外。最后社工总会问我们：什么安排对我爸最合适？那是什么样？

turns.en: And he would ultimately have the final say. So I think it's really important to talk to your loved one and see what are they open to? Because if you have a loved one that says, I'm not going anywhere but home, maybe save yourself the time and the energy of talking to the social worker about a placement in a nursing rehabilitation center or some other care setting if your loved one is certainly not going to have any buy-in to that.
turns.zh: 但拍板权最终在我爸手里。所以我觉得最重要的是先问你的亲人他们能接受什么。如果亲人说“除了家我哪儿都不去”，那就别费劲跟社工谈什么转去护理疗养机构或其他照护场所——因为他们根本不会配合。

turns.en: And then just know that you're sort of at the whim of those places of do they want to have an open bed? Two, do they have the staff to care for what's going on in your parents' life?
turns.zh: 然后要知道，你基本任这些机构摆布：第一，他们有没有空床位？第二，他们有没有人手能照护你父母的情况？

turns.en: And do they actually want to take care of that person? I mean, we've talked about my dad being a difficult patient and we faced a situation at one point where there were no places that would take him.
turns.zh: 第三，他们到底愿不愿意接这个人？我们说过我爸是个“难搞的病人”，我们一度遇到过没有任何机构愿意收他的境地。

turns.en: So he ended up being in the hospital for a long period of time even though he didn't necessarily medically need to be there. And the last thing I'll say on this if you don't feel that it's a safe discharge, like say they want to go home, they're resistant somewhere and maybe somewhere won't take them, you can always say it's an unsafe discharge and that will hold things up for a little bit.
turns.zh: 所以即便医学上不必，他在医院住了很长一段时间。关于这点我最后说一句：如果你觉得出院不安全——比如他们要回家、某处拒收、或哪儿都不收——你可以主张这是不安全出院（unsafe discharge），能拖住一阵。

turns.en: But if they have somewhere to go, eventually they are going to send them there. So one thing I liked about the book is that you had some concrete tips for dealing with healthcare professionals, communicating with them.
turns.zh: 但只要有地方可去，医院早晚会把人放走。书中我很喜欢的一点，是你给了很多与医疗专业人员沟通的具体技巧。

turns.en: I remember racing over to the hospital when my parents would be in the hospital because the doctors would do their rounds, first thing in the morning or whatever.
turns.zh: 我记得我父母住院时，我都会一大早赶到医院，因为医生查房都在早上或什么时间。

turns.en: What tips do you have for people attempting to communicate with individuals overseeing parents' care? Yeah, so that's an excellent one. Doctors do tend to round in the morning.
turns.zh: 对于想和父母医疗团队沟通的人，你有什么技巧？这一条就非常好。医生确实倾向早上查房。

turns.en: So I think if you're not there and you're not able to be there for rounds, don't call first thing in the morning. You're not going to get a call anytime soon in most cases.
turns.zh: 所以如果你不在场、赶不上查房，别一大早就打电话。多数情况下，你短时间等不到回电。

turns.en: I usually call in the afternoon after they've done their rounds and you have some updates. The other thing I would say is you don't necessarily have to always reach out to the doctors.
turns.zh: 我通常下午打，查房结束、有新进展之后。另一点是：你不一定非得只找医生。

turns.en: I found a lot of valuable information from medical assistants or medical aides from nurses. They're often seeing your loved one more often and can give you a better sense of how they're doing that particular day.
turns.zh: 我发现医疗助理、护工、护士那里常有非常有用的信息。他们见你亲人的频率更高，能告诉你当天的真实状态。

turns.en: They won't necessarily provide all the medical updates. Sometimes they can, but just sort of generally, how are they feeling? I also find that if you have a one-pager of current meds, recent hospitalizations, medical conditions, anything like that, it can be helpful to reference in difficult scenarios because there's a lot going on at that time.
turns.zh: 他们未必能给出全部医疗进展，有时能，但至少能笼统说说今天感觉怎么样。我还发现，如果有一张一页纸的清单，列着当前用药、近期住院、病症等，在兵荒马乱时引用起来特别有用，因为那种时候乱成一团。

turns.en: If you have that one-pager, you can reference it, and that way you're not forgetting anything. If someone, for example, if your loved one has interactions with a certain med or they don't do well under this scenario or they get tired in the later part of the day, something like that, you can communicate that.
turns.zh: 有这一页纸你就不怕遗漏。比如你的亲人与某种药物有相互作用、在某种情形下状态不好、下午容易犯困——这些你都能及时传达。

turns.en: So hopefully they can get better care throughout their stay. Your dad was kind of in and out of several different care settings toward the end of his life.
turns.zh: 这样一来，希望他们住院期间能得到更好的照护。你父亲在生命最后阶段辗转于好几个不同的照护机构。

turns.en: What did you learn from that experience, and what advice do you have for adult children who are trying to help their parents find an appropriate setting for assisted living?
turns.zh: 那段经历你学到了什么？对正在帮父母找合适辅助生活（assisted living）机构的成年子女，你有什么建议？

turns.en: I think the biggest thing here is not all care is created equally, and so it's really important to actually go view the facilities and make sure that they have really looked at your person's medical file and have the capabilities to do this.
turns.zh: 我觉得最大的一点是：照护质量参差不齐。所以一定要亲自去看设施，确认他们真的审阅过你亲人的病历、并且有足够的照护能力。

turns.en: I give the example in the book that my dad went to assisted living for 48 hours and then was kicked out. I was reassured when he went that they had reviewed his medical file, and I had trusted that.
turns.zh: 我在书里举了个例子：我爸去一家辅助生活机构，48 小时就被劝退了。入住时他们向我保证已经看过他的病历，我当时信了。

turns.en: Turns out I shouldn't really have trusted that because I don't think they actually looked. For me, it was a relatively minor thing that happened.
turns.zh: 结果我本不该信——我觉得他们根本没看。在我这里，那本来算相对小的问题。

turns.en: I mean, my dad acted inappropriately, but to be kicked out that quickly and out $5,000 after we spent a week trying to get him moved in and I flew across the country to help make this happen, it was a really frustrating experience and made me very angry at that assisted living place.
turns.zh: 我爸行为确实不当，但这么快被赶出来、白花 5000 美元——我们花了一整个星期折腾入住，我还专程飞越半个国家去帮忙——那段经历令人沮丧，让我对那家机构非常愤怒。

turns.en: So I would look up reviews, I would talk to friends, reach out to your elder care consultant. If it's a nursing home or rehab, look on Medicare.gov for reviews of that and go to the facility, not necessarily for a tour, but just drop in and see how do things look and start talking to residents there.
turns.zh: 所以我会查评价、问朋友、联系你的老年照护顾问。如果是疗养院或康复机构，上 Medicare.gov 看评价。再就是要亲自去 facility——不一定是预约参观，就是突然登门，看看现场是什么样子，和住户聊一聊。

turns.en: What's their experience been like? I think that is a very valuable thing because it's very hard and time intensive and expensive to get moved in and I know lots of people will move loved ones out of certain assisted living facilities or other living environments if a place is purchased or care goes downhill or something like that and it can be sort of a shocking thing to your parent to have to move during that
turns.zh: 他们的体验如何？我觉得这非常宝贵，因为入住又难、又费时间、又贵。我知道很多人会把亲人从某个辅助生活机构或居所搬出来——机构被收购、照护质量下滑、或别的原因——而对父母来说，这种被迫的搬家常常是当头一棒，

turns.en: and it's a hard reset that usually takes time. As you mentioned, Elliott, for a lot of older adults staying put in their homes is the default and I know that for adult children that can be a source of a lot of frustration especially if the home doesn't seem like a safe or appropriate place for the parent to be.
turns.zh: 是一次艰难的重启，通常需要时间恢复。Elliott，正如你所说，很多老年人默认就是要待在自己家里。我知道这对成年子女可能是巨大的挫败来源，尤其当那个家看起来已经不适合父母安全居住时。

turns.en: Do you have any advice for adult children navigating this particular situation? I'm going to go back to just encourage as much conversation as you can early on and see what are the qualities at home that are important to them because I think it's important to figure out what it is they enjoy about living there to see if those qualities can exist somewhere else or at a different time in the healthcare journey
turns.zh: 对应对这种情况的成年子女，你有什么建议？我还回到那句话：尽量趁早多沟通，弄清楚家里对他们重要的到底是什么。我觉得搞明白他们喜欢 home 的哪些品质，才能判断这些品质能不能在别处、或在医疗历程的下一个阶段继续存在。

turns.en: and maybe opening the question of like under what scenarios would they be open to moving to a different place, right? If they say, never, and that's the end of the conversation, you might just have to figure out for yourself, okay, I'm going to set the boundary of I'm willing to help them but they're going to figure out how to live at home and a lot of this comes back to how do I set these boundaries
turns.zh: 也可以把问题打开：什么样的情形下他们愿意搬去别的地方？如果他们说“绝不”，对话就结束了，那你可能只能自己拿定主意：好，我愿意帮忙，但他们要自己想办法在家生活。很多事最终都回到：我怎么设定边界。

turns.en: and in my dad's situation, this was really, really hard to do and we just kept trying to get him to move for as long as possible but eventually we just ran out of energy and we let him fail at home and that's something the elder care consultant helped us with, sort of reconciling is as hard to do but at that point, your loved one will reach out and that's what ended up happening to my dad is he failed so badly at home,
turns.zh: 我爸的情况，做到这点真的非常非常难。我们一直在努力劝他搬家，劝到精疲力竭。最后我们实在没能量了，就让他在家里“失败”一次——这也是老年照护顾问帮我们消化的，很难。但到那个份上，你的亲人会反过来求助。我爸就是这样，他在家里彻底撑不住了，

turns.en: he called me in tears and my dad never cried asking me to help him find a place to live so it can be effective and I know it sounds cruel but you also can't burn yourself out trying to get them to do something that they don't want to do you can't care about it more than your loved one Yeah, so I wanted to follow up on that issue of burnout and the whole caregiving journey can be both physically and emotionally draining
turns.zh: 打电话给我，哭着求我帮他找地方住——我爸从来没哭过。所以这招有效。我知道这听起来很残忍，但你不能为了逼他们做不愿做的事而把自己烧干。你不能比你的亲人更在意这件事。是啊，我想接着聊聊“耗竭”这个问题。照护之旅在体力和情感上都极其消耗。

turns.en: the book includes some tips for making caregiving slightly less painful whether it's taking time out to laugh or trying to enjoy quality time with your parent even if they're declining in health can you share any other ideas for things that people can do to kind of protect their own sanity and happiness while they're also advocating for their loved one?
turns.zh: 书里给了一些让照护稍微不那么痛苦的建议——比如留点时间笑一笑，或者趁父母健康尚在享受共处时光。还有什么办法能让人们在为亲人奔走的同时，守护自己的心智和快乐？

turns.en: Yeah, this is a really challenging one to do I think as much as you can hire and outsource certain things which usually when you start you don't want to do any of that but as you get farther along you realize it's just a reality that you're going to have to do so if you can do that earlier it hopefully will give you more energy and that could be as simple as hiring an attorney hiring a financial planner
turns.zh: 这真的很难做到。我觉得尽可能雇佣和外包——刚开始你什么都不想假手于人，但越往后越明白这是现实。越早接受，越能保住你的能量。哪怕只是请个律师、请个理财规划师、

turns.en: elder care consultant daily money manager nursing aides whatever it is whatever your pain points are or things that you don't like to do and that your loved one's willing to accept help hire that can be helpful also schedule time for yourself I know that's easier said than done but I think it's really important as you go along in your journey that you just have to take the time that you outsource for yourself
turns.zh: 老年照护顾问、日常账务管理员、护理助理——什么都行。哪个是你的痛点、哪件事你不愿做、而亲人也愿意接受帮助，就雇人做。还要给自己安排独处的时间。

turns.en: and set those boundaries with your loved ones I know I've said that a lot of times and I will just continue saying that too as many people who will listen but you have to set the boundaries that you are comfortable with your parents don't or your loved ones don't get to set those boundaries for you you get to set those boundaries and they may need to change over time I know they certainly did for my mom and me
turns.zh: 和亲人设好边界。我知道我把这话说了很多遍，对每一个愿意听的人我还是会继续说：你必须设定你自己觉得舒服的界限。你的父母或亲人不能替你把边界划了——边界由你来定，而且它们可能需要随时间调整。我知道我和妈妈之间就是这样，

turns.zh: 身边根本没有朋友家里是这个情况。所以我加入了一个线上年轻照护者互助小组。那对我帮助很大，因为大家人生阶段相似，父母的情况也相似。当朋友和家人无法体会你的处境时，那里是一个可以倾诉的地方。对我来说，它给了我社群感和归属感。尽可能找线下的，
